news.headline: Irving finished with 14 points (7-20 FG, 0-4 3Pt), two rebounds, two assists and three steals across 28 minutes in Friday's 112-100 win over the Jazz.
news.story: Irving struggled offensively, shooting just 35 percent from the field while missing all four three-point attempts, but the three steals helped salvage some fantasy value. Irving's scoring and playmaking remain major fantasy assets, though his production can fluctuate when his perimeter shooting and assist numbers are limited. He's had more than five assists in just two of his seven appearances this season and has scored over 20 points just three times.

news.headline: Irving (illness) is available for Friday's game against Utah.
news.story: The Mavericks previously added Irving to the injury report as probable with an illness, so there was little doubt regarding his status. The star guard should be able to handle his typical workload Friday, provided he faces no in-game setbacks with the ailment.

news.headline: Irving (illness) is probable for Friday's game against Utah.
news.story: Irving presumably woke up Friday morning under the weather. The issue isn't expected to prevent the star guard from playing, and Irving is likely to go through pregame warmups before Dallas confirms his status.

news.story: VanVleet supplied efficient perimeter scoring, recording four three-pointers for the third time in his last five outings while contributing four assists. His established role, both as a playmaker and scorer, and consistent three-point volume continue to provide fantasy utility, particularly in category formats emphasizing assists and perimeter shooting. news.headline: VanVleet (knee) isn't listed on the injury report for Monday's game against the Celtics.
news.story: VanVleet took the night off Saturday, which was the second night of a back-to-back set, but will return to action Monday. The veteran has looked solid coming back from an ACL tear, averaging 13.0 points, 6.4 assists, 4.0 rebounds and 1.8 steals in 30.6 minutes per game across his first five appearances.

news.headline: VanVleet (knee) won't play Saturday against the Thunder.
news.story: It's the second night of a back-to-back set, so VanVleet will receive his standard maintenance day, but he should return for Monday's meeting with the Celtics. Reed Sheppard (back) is also out for Saturday's game, so Marcus Smart could draw the start at point guard, and Amen Thompson should see some increased playmaking responsibilities.

news.headline: Flagg registered 21 points (7-16 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 6-6 FT), 10 rebounds, seven assists, three steals and a block across 33 minutes in Friday's 112-100 win over the Jazz.
news.story: Flagg delivered an outstanding all-around performance, finishing three assists shy of a triple-double while helping Dallas take control in the third quarter. His three steals further enhanced an already impressive fantasy line, demonstrating his ability to contribute across multiple categories. Flagg's substantial playing time and versatile statistical production continue to establish him as a valuable fantasy asset with elite upside across all formats. news.headline: Flagg notched 19 points (7-19 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 5-7 FT), 10 rebounds and five assists in 40 minutes during Wednesday's 112-111 loss to the Spurs.
news.story: The double-double was the second of the season for Flagg, and his first involving rebounds. The second-year star is taking a step forward from his Rookie of the Year campaign, averaging 24.3 points, 6.3 boards, 6.3 assists, 2.1 steals, 1.0 threes and 0.9 blocks over seven games, and there's still plenty of room for growth in his skills. Flagg is shooting just 21.2 percent from beyond the arc.

news.headline: Flagg ended Monday's 115-100 loss to the Kings with 17 points (3-19 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 11-11 FT), four rebounds, six assists and two steals in 40 minutes.
news.story: With Kyrie Irving resting Monday, the Kings were able to devote most of their defensive attention to Flagg and hold the second-year superstar in check from the field. Flagg is still off to an excellent start overall, averaging 25.2 points, 6.5 assists and 5.7 rebounds per game so far this season.

news.headline: Reed racked up 11 points (5-6 FG, 1-2 FT), five rebounds, four assists, two blocks and two steals across 28 minutes during Monday's 124-91 victory over the Hornets.
news.story: Reed turned in another strong two-way performance, filling in for the injured Jalen Duren (hamstring). In four appearances over the past week, he has been a top-30 asset in nine-category leagues, averaging 15.3 points, 5.5 rebounds, 0.8 three-pointers and 3.0 combined steals and blocks. The eventual return of Duren will certainly impact Reed's production. However, given how well the team has functioned with Reed as the starting center, there is a case to be made for him playing over John Collins, alongside Duren.

news.headline: Clingan closed with 24 points (9-12 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), 11 rebounds, one assist, three blocks and one steal over 29 minutes during Wednesday's 132-119 victory over Phoenix.
news.story: The double-double was the second straight for Clingan, while the 24 points were a season high for the third-year center. Clingan also recorded multiple rejections for the fourth time in seven games, and so far in 2026-27, he's averaging 12.0 points, 10.6 boards, 2.4 blocks, 1.6 assists and 1.0 threes while shooting 56.9 percent from the field and a surprising 46.7 percent from long distance.

news.headline: Clingan delivered 17 points (8-16 FG, 1-3 3Pt), 18 rebounds, three assists and four blocks across 32 minutes in Monday's 118-110 win over the Nuggets.
news.story: Clingan delivered an outstanding fantasy performance, grabbing nine offensive rebounds while providing elite rim protection against Denver's frontcourt led by none other than Nikola Jokic. Clingan's combination of rebounding volume and shot-blocking makes him an appealing option at center, and even though he's not likely to hover around the 15-point mark on a regular basis, his floor remains very high due to his two-way contributions.

news.headline: Acuff finished with 22 points (9-20 FG, 3-9 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds, eight assists and two steals in 33 minutes during Friday's 124-109 loss to San Antonio.
news.story: Acuff led the Kings in scoring and assists in another encouraging rookie performance. He needed 20 shots to get there, but his ability to create offense has made him one of the bright spots in a rough start for Sacramento. As the Kings lose more games, expect them to keep giving him the ball.

news.headline: Acuff finished Wednesday's 116-103 loss to the Lakers with 22 points (8-24 FG, 3-11 3Pt, 3-4 FT), three rebounds, 12 assists and two steals across 42 minutes.
news.story: Acuff struggled with his efficiency, needing 24 shots to reach 22 points, but he made up for it with a double-double. That extends his streak of games with at least five assists to six. The rookie's heavy usage and team-high 42 minutes make him a fantasy asset even on off shooting nights, though his efficiency could weigh on managers in category leagues.

news.story: Lendeborg combined efficient scoring with strong rebounding and rim protection, delivering one of his most complete performances of the season and ending just two boards shy of a double-double. news.story: Lendeborg continues to play at a high level for the Warriors, posting a third straight game with at least 15 points, a mark he's reached in seven of his nine appearances so far. Lendeborg should continue to operate as the Warriors' No. 2 option on offense behind Stephen Curry, and he's quickly rising up the Rookie of the Year rankings.

news.headline: Young finished with four points (1-6 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-3 FT), five rebounds, three assists and one steal in 28 minutes during Saturday's 114-75 loss to the Thunder.
news.story: Young turned in a lackluster all-around performance, delivering his lowest point total in a game since Nov. 4, 2024, when he recorded just two points in 23 minutes. The star floor general also delivered a season low in assists. In four outings so far this month, Young has averaged 15.0 points, 7.0 assists, 3.0 rebounds and 1.3 steals across 33.3 minutes per contest.

news.headline: Young registered 18 points (6-12 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 4-4 FT), two rebounds, six assists, one block and two steals over 34 minutes during Wednesday's 120-105 loss to the Hawks.
news.story: Young delivered a respectable offensive performance against his former team, shooting 50 percent from the field while contributing six assists. However, he committed four turnovers and couldn't prevent Washington from suffering a 15-point defeat. The veteran point guard continues to serve as a primary offensive facilitator for the Wizards, providing a reliable source of points and assists for fantasy managers.

news.headline: Green recorded two points (1-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 0-2 FT), six rebounds, 13 assists, two steals and two blocks across 34 minutes in Saturday's 126-119 overtime win over the Magic.
news.story: Green overcame a nearly nonexistent scoring contribution by delivering outstanding playmaking and defensive production. His season-high 13 assists and four combined defensive stats provided substantial category-league value, and it's worth noting he's now dished out double-digit assists in back-to-back games. Green's poor scoring numbers limit his upside, but there's no denying that he's compensating for that with strong numbers in other categories. Over his last five games, Green is averaging 2.6 points, 5.6 rebounds, 8.2 assists, 1.4 steals and 1.2 blocks per contest.

news.headline: Green (elbow) is available for Saturday's game against the Magic.
news.story: Green will power through the elbow issue and make himself available for Saturday's game. The 36-year-old forward is averaging 3.0 points, 5.0 rebounds, 7.0 assists and 1.8 stocks per contest this season.

news.headline: Green (elbow) is listed as questionable ahead of Saturday's game against Orlando.
news.story: Green is coming off an 11-assist performance in Thursday's 120-100 win over the Heat. He's in danger of missing his third contest of the 2026-27 campaign due to elbow inflammation. If Green is downgraded to out, Charles Bassey and Al Horford would likely split time at the five.

news.story: Johnson delivered his first career double-double, dominating the glass with 10 offensive rebounds while matching his season high in points. His impressive rebounding production came despite a relatively modest workload, highlighting his potential as an interior contributor. Johnson's fantasy appeal continues to grow, and he could be in line for an expanded role in Dallas' frontcourt as the season progresses. He has scored in double figures in three of his last five games, averaging 9.2 points and 6.0 boards per game over that stretch.

news.story: The Mavericks continue to bring the rookie first-rounder along slowly after Johnson missed the start of training camp. Until his restrictions are loosened, Johnson's fantasy upside will remain capped.

news.story: Making just his second start of the season -- both which have come in his last three games -- Mara capitalized on his opportunities with efficient interior scoring and strong rim protection. His three blocks were especially valuable for category-league managers, while eight rebounds and three assists added versatility to his performance. news.headline: Mara will start Saturday against the Wizards, Rylan Stiles of SI.com reports.
news.story: Mara will replace Jared McCain in the first unit for Saturday's game. In his previous start this season, Mara finished with nine points, five rebounds, two assists and three blocks over 25 minutes.

news.headline: Zubac notched 10 points (4-5 FG, 2-2 FT), 12 rebounds and five assists in 19 minutes during Saturday's 114-102 loss to the Nuggets.
news.story: Zubac recorded his second double-double of the season, and his first since returning from an ankle injury that cost him five games. He was dealing with some foul trouble, which may have contributed to him playing just 19 minutes. However, he appears to be trending in the right direction and should approach closer to 30 minutes per game in the not too distant future.

news.headline: Zubac produced one point (0-5 FG, 1-2 FT), four rebounds and two assists in 19 minutes during Wednesday's 107-103 win over the Grizzlies.
news.story: Zubac endured a miserable offensive showing, missing all five of his field-goal attempts and finishing with a team-worst minus-22 rating. The veteran center also failed to record a steal or block, while Indiana found more success with its reserve frontcourt options. Despite his established rebounding upside, Zubac's limited playing time and lack of production made this a particularly disappointing fantasy outing in his return from injury.

news.headline: Zubac (ankle) is available for Wednesday's game against the Grizzlies, Alex Golden of SI.com reports.
news.story: Zubac will return Wednesday after missing the last five games due to an ankle injury. While Zubac may see fewer minutes in his first game back from the layoff, his presence will likely result in Jay Huff retreating to the bench.

news.headline: Nesmith registered 16 points (7-16 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 0-1 FT), a rebound, two assists, three steals and a block across 30 minutes in Wednesday's 107-103 win over the Grizzlies.
news.story: Nesmith delivered the decisive three-pointer in the closing seconds, extending Indiana's lead after Memphis pulled within one point. His four combined defensive stats significantly boosted his fantasy production despite modest rebounding and playmaking totals. Nesmith's established playing time and defensive contributions support his value in category formats, although his scoring consistency is dependent on perimeter efficiency. He's trending in the right direction, scoring in double figures in five of his last six appearances.

news.headline: Nesmith (rest) is not listed on the injury report for Wednesday's game in Memphis.
news.story: Nesmith sat out Monday's 108-104 loss to the Hawks for rest purposes, but he'll be back in action Wednesday evening. Nesmith is averaging 12.2 points, 1.8 assists and 1.7 triples per game this season.

news.headline: Nesmith (rest) is sitting out Monday against Atlanta.
news.story: The Pacers are holding him out for left hamstring injury management, but this is a maintenance day and not a setback for the second leg of this back-to-back set. Kelly Oubre and Jarace Walker could see hefty workloads with so many Pacers sitting out.

news.headline: Banchero is expected to be sidelined for the next four-to-six weeks due to a right high-ankle sprain, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
news.story: Banchero left during Friday's loss against the Timberwolves due to an ankle injury, and follow-up tests have confirmed a high-ankle sprain for the fifth-year forward. With an extended absence expected, the Magic will have to rely more heavily on Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane offensively, and Tristan da Silva figures to be the top candidate to enter the Magic's starting lineup for as long as Banchero is sidelined.

news.headline: Banchero didn't check back in during the fourth quarter of Friday's 115-93 loss to the Timberwolves after being deemed doubtful to return. He finished with 14 points (5-11 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-4 FT), six rebounds, five assists and one steal across 26 minutes.
news.story: Banchero exited to the locker room in the third quarter after tweaking his right ankle. He briefly returned to action in the third but didn't see the floor in the fourth due to ankle soreness. The star forward can be considered questionable for Sunday's game at New York until the Magic offer an update on his status.

news.headline: Banchero is doubtful to return to Friday's game against the Timberwolves due to a sore right ankle, NBA reporter Marc Stein reports.
news.story: The Magic are currently down by 20-plus points with four minutes to go in the fourth quarter, so that may be impacting Orlando's decision to hold Banchero out of the remainder of the game. For now, Banchero should be considered questionable for Sunday's game in New York.

news.headline: Hyland amassed 19 points (7-13 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds, four assists and one steal across 16 minutes during Wednesday's 117-107 victory over Houston.
news.story: Hyland scored at least 19 points for the second time in the past four games, having now also scored double-digit points in four of the past five games. While he is being asked to do more on the offensive end, his production does seem somewhat unsustainable, especially given his playing time. In four appearances over the past week, he has averaged just 16.0 minutes per game, typically not enough to maintain standard-league relevance.

news.headline: Hyland racked up 19 points (8-16 FG, 3-9 3Pt), eight assists and one steal across 20 minutes during Friday's 127-101 victory over the Clippers.
news.story: Hyland finished just two assists shy of a double-double and recorded his second straight game with double-digit points and over 15 minutes of action. It's still early, but the early signs show Hyland could be in line for a bigger role in the backcourt with Anthony Edwards (knee) sidelined for the foreseeable future.

news.headline: Fantasy Hoops: The Timberwolves players to add in wake of Anthony Edwards injury
news.story: Minnesota Timberwolves guard Anthony Edwards was putting up some of the best numbers of his career before Tuesday's news. Through four games, he averaged 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds and 3.5 assists while shooting 48% from the field. He even scored 47 points in 41 minutes against the Cleveland Cavaliers on Monday despite dealing with knee pain. Now Edwards is scheduled for arthroscopic surgery on his right knee Thursday and could miss around two months. A more definitive return timeline should come after the procedure. news.headline: George (illness) has been downgraded to questionable for Sunday's game against Minnesota.
news.story: George presumably woke up under the weather before being a late addition to the injury report. If the star point guard is unable to suit up, Darryn Peterson could see additional on-ball duties. Additionally, Isaiah Collier and Svi Mykhailiuk would be candidates for increased playing time.

news.headline: George tallied 16 points (6-13 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 3-4 FT), six rebounds, nine assists and a block across 32 minutes in Friday's 112-100 loss to the Mavericks.
news.story: George narrowly missed a double-double, providing strong playmaking production while contributing six rebounds. George's consistent playmaking supports his fantasy value, but his overall ceiling depends on improving efficiency and limiting mistakes -- he's had at least three turnovers in his last four games. Overall, George is averaging a solid 21.3 points, 4.2 rebounds and 6.2 assists per game this season while shooting 45.5 percent from the floor and 32.1 percent from deep.

news.headline: George registered 39 points (14-26 FG, 2-9 3Pt, 9-13 FT), two rebounds, nine assists, four steals and one block over 44 minutes in Wednesday's 120-113 overtime loss to the Pelicans.
news.story: George had been seriously struggling in his previous two outings, combining for 15 points on 5-for-22 shooting, but he busted out of his funk in a big way Wednesday. He nearly delivered a game-winning dagger for Utah, but his stepback jumper left his hand just a second too late, and the team wasn't able to hang on in overtime. The Jazz have opened the season 1-7.

news.headline: Jaquez posted 18 points (7-16 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 0-2 FT), two rebounds, two assists and a steal across 31 minutes in Wednesday's 109-102 loss to the Celtics.
news.story: Jaquez supplied Milwaukee with valuable perimeter scoring, converting four of six three-point attempts while maintaining a substantial offensive role. However, his limited rebounding and playmaking restricted his overall fantasy production. His 31-minute workload was encouraging, and he's averaged 16.8 points, 6.6 rebounds and 2.8 assists in 28.4 minutes across eight appearances.

news.headline: Jaquez ended with 19 points (8-17 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT), eight rebounds, two assists and one steal in 28 minutes during Monday's 112-100 loss to the Timberwolves.
news.story: Jaquez finished second on Milwaukee in scoring behind Tyler Herro and was one of the team's few reliable offensive contributors in a game in which the Bucks shot just 38.4 percent from the field. He has established himself as a regular starter, and his ability to contribute across multiple categories gives him a solid fantasy foundation despite Milwaukee's early-season struggles.

news.headline: Jaquez supplied 19 points (7-13 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, two assists and one steal across 27 minutes in Wednesday's 132-100 loss to Houston.
news.story: After scoring a season-low eight points on 4-of-13 shooting in Monday's win over Indiana, Jaquez bounced back Wednesday, albeit in a losing effort. The 25-year-old swingman finished as Milwaukee's second-leading scorer, knocking down a season-best three triples. He's scored at least 19 points in four of his five regular-season appearances and should continue playing a sizable role for the Bucks alongside Tyler Herro.

news.headline: Antetokounmpo tallied 20 points (7-13 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 5-7 FT), 14 rebounds and four assists across 31 minutes during Thursday's 120-100 loss to the Warriors.
news.story: Antetokounmpo now has six straight regular-season outings with a double-double. He's been stellar to begin his tenure in Miami, and prior to Thursday night's defeat, the Heat had won three of the previous four games. Over Antetokounmpo's last six contests, he's averaging 26.8 points, 15.0 rebounds and 6.8 assists to go along with 1.3 blocks.

news.headline: Antetokounmpo (wrist) is available for Thursday's game against the Warriors, Anthony Chiang of the Miami Herald reports.
news.story: With Miami on the second night of a back-to-back, Antetokounmpo's availability removes any immediate concern about the wrist issue affecting his status Thursday. The star forward should remain in his usual role, though it's worth noting his wrist was heavily taped Wednesday against the Clippers, per Chiang.

news.headline: Embiid (foot) is available for Sunday's game against the Bulls.
news.story: Embiid will avoid his third absence of the 2026-27 campaign. The 32-year-old hasn't played up to his usual standards in his eight regular-season appearances, averaging a career-low 17.9 points over 32.4 minutes per contest while shooting a miserable 10.7 percent from behind the arc.

news.headline: Embiid (foot) is probable for Sunday's game against the Bulls.
news.story: Embiid continues to work through plantar fasciitis in his right foot. Philadelphia has kept their star center on an injury management routine, and with Embiid being listed as probable to suit up versus Chicago, he's likely to be active and reprise his starting role for the 8-2 76ers.

news.headline: Embiid chipped in 26 points (8-18 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 10-10 FT), 15 rebounds, two assists and one steal across 33 minutes during Wednesday's 112-106 win over Detroit.
news.story: Embiid controlled the interior, pulling down four offensive rebounds while converting all 10 of his free-throw attempts. The veteran center delivered a strong double-double despite struggling from beyond the arc, providing Philadelphia with a reliable presence in the paint. His 33-minute workload was also encouraging for fantasy managers monitoring his availability and playing time.

news.headline: Mitchell amassed 22 points (9-18 FG, 4-9 3Pt), two rebounds, eight assists and one steal over 38 minutes during Thursday's 120-100 loss to the Warriors.
news.story: Although Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo led the Heat's offense, Mitchell continues to thrive as a reliable third scoring option and primary facilitator. This 22-point output matched his previous season-high mark, and he's reached the 15-point plateau in six of his nine appearances. He's averaging career-high marks in points (16.1) and assists (8.2) per game so far.

news.headline: Mitchell closed with 11 points (5-13 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 1-1 FT), two rebounds, 10 assists, one block and four steals in 43 minutes during Wednesday's 117-116 overtime win over the Clippers.
news.story: Mitchell's shot wasn't falling from deep, but he logged a team-high 43 minutes and made up for it with a double-double and five combined steals-plus-blocks. He's now scored in double figures in all eight appearances this season, and his playmaking has been a steady source of fantasy value. As long as he's seeing this kind of workload, he should be rostered in most formats.

news.headline: Mitchell closed Monday's 138-117 loss to the Lakers with 15 points (5-5 FG, 4-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), seven assists and one block across 29 minutes.
news.story: Mitchell continues to flourish in the early going, having scored in double digits in each of his first seven appearances while dishing out at least seven dimes in five of them. On the year, the point guard has averaged 16.0 points, 8.0 assists and 1.0 steals in 33.4 minutes per game.

news.headline: Jones ended Wednesday's 117-116 overtime loss to Miami with 12 points (5-11 FG, 2-5 3Pt), eight rebounds, one assist, three blocks and one steal across 37 minutes.
news.story: Jones returned to the starting lineup after missing Monday's game with a right knee injury he suffered Sunday. He handled a full workload and was a factor on the defensive end, finishing with four combined steals-plus-blocks. He's a useful source of defensive stats when healthy, though his limited offensive role caps his upside.

news.headline: Jones (knee) has been removed from the injury report ahead of Wednesday's game against the Heat, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
news.story: Jones will be back in action Wednesday following a one-game stint on the sidelines, which should result in Kobe Sanders returning to the second unit. Jones is averaging 11.5 points, 4.8 rebounds, 2.2 triples and 1.2 steals per game this season.

news.headline: Jones (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Raptors.
news.story: Jones exited Sunday's loss to the Warriors and did not return due to a right knee injury. He's now listed on the injury report with right knee soreness, and the veteran forward's next chance to play will come Wednesday against Miami. In the meantime, Kobe Sanders, Baba Miller and Gradey Dick are candidates for increased playing time.

news.headline: Curry popped off for 41 points (13-19 FG, 5-10 3Pt, 10-10 FT), six rebounds and six assists over 36 minutes in Saturday's 126-119 overtime win over Orlando.
news.story: This was Curry's second 40-plus-point performance of the season, and through his first eight games, he has more total points (250) than minutes played (237). This was also Curry's 16th 40-plus-point performance since turning 35, putting him ahead of LeBron James for the most such games in NBA history. He'll look to keep his foot on the gas pedal Monday against the Pelicans.

news.story: Murray was efficient from inside the arc and finished as Denver's third-leading scorer Saturday. The star floor general also tied for the team lead in assists, dishing out at least six dimes for a third consecutive contest. news.headline: Murray finished with 14 points (4-11 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds, seven assists and a steal across 28 minutes in Wednesday's 128-109 win over the Raptors.

His reduced playing time reflected Denver's comfortable second-half advantage, so fantasy managers shouldn't worry too much about the fact that he didn't reach the 30-minute threshold for the first time this season.

news.headline: Jackson (groin) is available for Wednesday's game against the Heat, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
news.story: Jackson was a late addition to the injury report Wednesday, though he'll ditch his questionable tag and suit up. The big man posted 19 points, eight rebounds and two assists across 26 minutes off the bench in Monday's loss to Toronto, and he'll continue operating with the second unit Wednesday.

news.headline: Jackson is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Heat with left groin soreness, per Law Murray of The Athletic.
news.story: Jackson is a late addition to the injury report, which is a bad sign for his chances of playing Wednesday. If Jackson is ultimately downgraded to out, Brook Lopez would likely remain in the starting lineup.

news.story: The former Hornet has quickly gotten comfortable in a Suns jersey. Bridges has scored at least 16 points in five straight games, averaging 19.2 points, 7.6 boards, 3.4 assists, 2.6 threes and 1.8 steals, draining multiple threes in each of those contests and shooting 38.2 percent from long distance.

news.headline: Bridges had 21 points (7-14 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 4-5 FT), six rebounds, three assists, one block and four steals over 35 minutes during Monday's 116-113 loss to the Warriors.
news.story: Bridges delivered one of his strongest all-around performances of the young season, finishing second on Phoenix in scoring while leading the team with four steals. He also connected on three triples and committed just one turnover, providing valuable production across multiple fantasy categories. Bridges continues to handle a substantial workload in the Suns' starting lineup.

news.headline: Gordon notched 15 points (4-9 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 5-5 FT), four rebounds and five assists in 29 minutes during Friday's 127-120 win over the Suns.
news.story: Gordon was steady in the victory, and the forward was one of five Nuggets starters to reach double figures. His physicality on both ends remains a key piece of Denver's starting group. He'll look to keep it rolling Monday against the Trail Blazers.

news.headline: Gordon registered 15 points (3-10 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 7-8 FT), 11 rebounds, three assists and a steal across 31 minutes in Wednesday's 104-91 win over the Pelicans.
news.story: Gordon compensated for a difficult shooting performance by collecting 11 rebounds and converting seven free throws. Gordon's ability to contribute on the glass and from the perimeter gives him useful fantasy versatility, although his scoring remains dependent on opportunities alongside Denver's primary offensive options. news.story: Quickley was a late addition to the injury report and is dealing with some tightness. Presumably, the Raptors are considering a maintenance day here. Jamal Shead would be the next man up for Toronto.

news.headline: Banchero is expected to be sidelined for the next four-to-six weeks due to a right high-ankle sprain, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
news.story: Banchero left during Friday's loss against the Timberwolves due to an ankle injury, and follow-up tests have confirmed a high-ankle sprain for the fifth-year forward. With an extended absence expected, the Magic will have to rely more heavily on Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane offensively, and Tristan da Silva figures to be the top candidate to enter the Magic's starting lineup for as long as Banchero is sidelined.

news.headline: Banchero didn't check back in during the fourth quarter of Friday's 115-93 loss to the Timberwolves after being deemed doubtful to return. He finished with 14 points (5-11 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-4 FT), six rebounds, five assists and one steal across 26 minutes.
news.story: Banchero exited to the locker room in the third quarter after tweaking his right ankle. He briefly returned to action in the third but didn't see the floor in the fourth due to ankle soreness. The star forward can be considered questionable for Sunday's game at New York until the Magic offer an update on his status.

news.headline: Banchero is doubtful to return to Friday's game against the Timberwolves due to a sore right ankle, NBA reporter Marc Stein reports.
news.story: The Magic are currently down by 20-plus points with four minutes to go in the fourth quarter, so that may be impacting Orlando's decision to hold Banchero out of the remainder of the game. For now, Banchero should be considered questionable for Sunday's game in New York.

news.headline: Nesmith registered 16 points (7-16 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 0-1 FT), a rebound, two assists, three steals and a block across 30 minutes in Wednesday's 107-103 win over the Grizzlies.
news.story: Nesmith delivered the decisive three-pointer in the closing seconds, extending Indiana's lead after Memphis pulled within one point. His four combined defensive stats significantly boosted his fantasy production despite modest rebounding and playmaking totals. Nesmith's established playing time and defensive contributions support his value in category formats, although his scoring consistency is dependent on perimeter efficiency. He's trending in the right direction, scoring in double figures in five of his last six appearances.

news.headline: Nesmith (rest) is not listed on the injury report for Wednesday's game in Memphis.
news.story: Nesmith sat out Monday's 108-104 loss to the Hawks for rest purposes, but he'll be back in action Wednesday evening. Nesmith is averaging 12.2 points, 1.8 assists and 1.7 triples per game this season.

news.headline: Nesmith (rest) is sitting out Monday against Atlanta.
news.story: The Pacers are holding him out for left hamstring injury management, but this is a maintenance day and not a setback for the second leg of this back-to-back set. Kelly Oubre and Jarace Walker could see hefty workloads with so many Pacers sitting out.

news.story: Making just his second start of the season -- both which have come in his last three games -- Mara capitalized on his opportunities with efficient interior scoring and strong rim protection. Flagg's substantial playing time and versatile statistical production continue to establish him as a valuable fantasy asset with elite upside across all formats. news.headline: Flagg notched 19 points (7-19 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 5-7 FT), 10 rebounds and five assists in 40 minutes during Wednesday's 112-111 loss to the Spurs.
news.story: The double-double was the second of the season for Flagg, and his first involving rebounds. The second-year star is taking a step forward from his Rookie of the Year campaign, averaging 24.3 points, 6.3 boards, 6.3 assists, 2.1 steals, 1.0 threes and 0.9 blocks over seven games, and there's still plenty of room for growth in his skills. Flagg is shooting just 21.2 percent from beyond the arc.

news.headline: Flagg ended Monday's 115-100 loss to the Kings with 17 points (3-19 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 11-11 FT), four rebounds, six assists and two steals in 40 minutes.
news.story: With Kyrie Irving resting Monday, the Kings were able to devote most of their defensive attention to Flagg and hold the second-year superstar in check from the field. Flagg is still off to an excellent start overall, averaging 25.2 points, 6.5 assists and 5.7 rebounds per game so far this season.

news.headline: Acuff finished with 22 points (9-20 FG, 3-9 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds, eight assists and two steals in 33 minutes during Friday's 124-109 loss to San Antonio.
news.story: Acuff led the Kings in scoring and assists in another encouraging rookie performance. He needed 20 shots to get there, but his ability to create offense has made him one of the bright spots in a rough start for Sacramento. As the Kings lose more games, expect them to keep giving him the ball.

news.headline: Acuff finished Wednesday's 116-103 loss to the Lakers with 22 points (8-24 FG, 3-11 3Pt, 3-4 FT), three rebounds, 12 assists and two steals across 42 minutes.
news.story: Acuff struggled with his efficiency, needing 24 shots to reach 22 points, but he made up for it with a double-double. That extends his streak of games with at least five assists to six. The rookie's heavy usage and team-high 42 minutes make him a fantasy asset even on off shooting nights, though his efficiency could weigh on managers in category leagues.

news.story: The double-double was the second straight for Clingan, while the 24 points were a season high for the third-year center. news.story: Clingan delivered an outstanding fantasy performance, grabbing nine offensive rebounds while providing elite rim protection against Denver's frontcourt led by none other than Nikola Jokic. Clingan's combination of rebounding volume and shot-blocking makes him an appealing option at center, and even though he's not likely to hover around the 15-point mark on a regular basis, his floor remains very high due to his two-way contributions.

news.story: Green overcame a nearly nonexistent scoring contribution by delivering outstanding playmaking and defensive production. His season-high 13 assists and four combined defensive stats provided substantial category-league value, and it's worth noting he's now dished out double-digit assists in back-to-back games. Green's poor scoring numbers limit his upside, but there's no denying that he's compensating for that with strong numbers in other categories. Over his last five games, Green is averaging 2.6 points, 5.6 rebounds, 8.2 assists, 1.4 steals and 1.2 blocks per contest.

news.headline: Green (elbow) is available for Saturday's game against the Magic.
news.story: Green will power through the elbow issue and make himself available for Saturday's game. The 36-year-old forward is averaging 3.0 points, 5.0 rebounds, 7.0 assists and 1.8 stocks per contest this season.

news.story: Green is coming off an 11-assist performance in Thursday's 120-100 win over the Heat. He's in danger of missing his third contest of the 2026-27 campaign due to elbow inflammation. If Green is downgraded to out, Charles Bassey and Al Horford would likely split time at the five.

news.story: VanVleet supplied efficient perimeter scoring, recording four three-pointers for the third time in his last five outings while contributing four assists. His established role, both as a playmaker and scorer, and consistent three-point volume continue to provide fantasy utility, particularly in category formats emphasizing assists and perimeter shooting. news.story: VanVleet took the night off Saturday, which was the second night of a back-to-back set, but will return to action Monday. The veteran has looked solid coming back from an ACL tear, averaging 13.0 points, 6.4 assists, 4.0 rebounds and 1.8 steals in 30.6 minutes per game across his first five appearances.

news.headline: VanVleet (knee) won't play Saturday against the Thunder.
news.story: It's the second night of a back-to-back set, so VanVleet will receive his standard maintenance day, but he should return for Monday's meeting with the Celtics. Reed Sheppard (back) is also out for Saturday's game, so Marcus Smart could draw the start at point guard, and Amen Thompson should see some increased playmaking responsibilities.

news.headline: Zubac notched 10 points (4-5 FG, 2-2 FT), 12 rebounds and five assists in 19 minutes during Saturday's 114-102 loss to the Nuggets.
news.story: Zubac recorded his second double-double of the season, and his first since returning from an ankle injury that cost him five games. He was dealing with some foul trouble, which may have contributed to him playing just 19 minutes. However, he appears to be trending in the right direction and should approach closer to 30 minutes per game in the not too distant future.

news.headline: Zubac produced one point (0-5 FG, 1-2 FT), four rebounds and two assists in 19 minutes during Wednesday's 107-103 win over the Grizzlies.
news.story: Zubac endured a miserable offensive showing, missing all five of his field-goal attempts and finishing with a team-worst minus-22 rating. The veteran center also failed to record a steal or block, while Indiana found more success with its reserve frontcourt options. Despite his established rebounding upside, Zubac's limited playing time and lack of production made this a particularly disappointing fantasy outing in his return from injury.

news.headline: Zubac (ankle) is available for Wednesday's game against the Grizzlies, Alex Golden of SI.com reports.
news.story: Zubac will return Wednesday after missing the last five games due to an ankle injury. While Zubac may see fewer minutes in his first game back from the layoff, his presence will likely result in Jay Huff retreating to the bench.

news.headline: Irving finished with 14 points (7-20 FG, 0-4 3Pt), two rebounds, two assists and three steals across 28 minutes in Friday's 112-100 win over the Jazz.
news.story: Irving struggled offensively, shooting just 35 percent from the field while missing all four three-point attempts, but the three steals helped salvage some fantasy value. Irving's scoring and playmaking remain major fantasy assets, though his production can fluctuate when his perimeter shooting and assist numbers are limited. He's had more than five assists in just two of his seven appearances this season and has scored over 20 points just three times.

news.headline: Irving (illness) is available for Friday's game against Utah.
news.story: The Mavericks previously added Irving to the injury report as probable with an illness, so there was little doubt regarding his status. The star guard should be able to handle his typical workload Friday, provided he faces no in-game setbacks with the ailment.

news.headline: Irving (illness) is probable for Friday's game against Utah.
news.story: Irving presumably woke up Friday morning under the weather. The issue isn't expected to prevent the star guard from playing, and Irving is likely to go through pregame warmups before Dallas confirms his status.

news.headline: Sengun finished with 26 points (12-15 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), seven rebounds, 10 assists, two blocks and two steals across 38 minutes during Monday's 109-93 win over Boston.
news.story: Sengun recorded his first double-double with points and assists while shooting a red-hot 80 percent from the field on 15 attempts. The scoring and dimes were both game highs, and he notched his first outing with multiple steals and blocks. Sengun turned it over just once, too, a season low for the big man. He now has nine or more assists in three consecutive games, and he'll continue providing all-around fantasy production for the 7-1 Rockets.

news.story: This was Burries' first career double-double, and he set career highs in points, rebounds and assists. Since entering the starting lineup, Burries has been averaging 13.0 points, 8.3 rebounds and 3.3 assists per game on 41.7 percent shooting from the field and 70.0 percent at the line.

news.story: The rookie made his first NBA start and immediately received a substantial offensive workload, although he struggled with his efficiency. news.headline: Hunter (illness) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Sunday's game against Miami.
news.story: Hunter didn't play in Friday's 124-109 loss to the Spurs, marking his first absence of the season. He will return Sunday versus the Heat, likely meaning Leaky Black will head back to the bench.

news.headline: Hunter (illness) is listed as out for Friday's game against San Antonio.
news.story: Hunter was listed as questionable but has now been ruled out for the first time this season. His next opportunity to play will come Sunday versus the Heat. With Hunter unavailable, Malik Monk might find his way into the starting lineup.

news.headline: Hunter is questionable for Friday against the Spurs due to an illness.
news.story: Hunter is a late addition to the injury report. If he doesn't suit up Friday, Malik Monk and Leaky Black should soak up more playing time for the Kings.

news.headline: Castle tallied 14 points (5-12 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds, five assists and a block across 24 minutes in Saturday's 125-103 win over the Trail Blazers.
news.story: Castle delivered another well-rounded performance, contributing as a rebounder and facilitator while also posting his fourth consecutive game with 14 or more points. Castle's ability to contribute across several categories supports a strong fantasy floor in most formats. He's averaging 16.5 points, 6.3 rebounds and 4.8 assists per game since going scoreless in a win over the Timberwolves on Oct. 31.

news.headline: Castle had 19 points (7-13 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 4-5 FT), three rebounds and seven assists over 28 minutes during Friday's 124-109 win over Sacramento.
news.story: Castle was San Antonio's most active playmaker, finishing with a team-high seven assists alongside his 19 points. The former Rookie of the Year keeps growing as a lead guard, and his pairing with Dylan Harper in the backcourt gives the Spurs two young ball-handlers who can attack the basket.

news.headline: Castle finished with 17 points (6-20 FG, 2-9 3Pt, 3-4 FT), 10 rebounds and three assists over 35 minutes during Wednesday's 112-111 victory over Dallas.
news.story: Victor Wembanyama didn't need a whole lot of help Wednesday, but Castle was one of three other Spurs to score in double digits en route to his first double-double of the season. The third-year guard has scored at least 14 points in seven of eight games to begin the campaign, averaging 15.0 points, 6.1 boards, 4.8 assists, 2.4 threes and 1.0 steals, but there's room for growth in those numbers, as his 39.0 percent shooting from the floor would be a career low.

news.headline: Watson provided 12 points (5-11 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), six rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal over 29 minutes during Saturday's 109-97 loss to the Knicks.
news.story: Watson racked up three stocks after failing to record any defensive statistics his last time out, and this was his second straight game without committing a single turnover. He's been a steady late-round producer on the season with averages of 11.3 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.6 blocks per game.

news.headline: Watson (hamstring) is available for Friday's meeting with the 76ers.
news.story: Watson is back after a two-game absence, and his return will likely shift Tyrese Proctor back to the second unit. Watson is averaging 10.8 points, 4.0 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 1.2 steals and 1.8 blocks per game this season.

news.headline: Watson (hamstring) is questionable for Friday's game against the 76ers.
news.story: Watson has missed his team's last two matchups due to a hamstring issue, and he's in danger of missing a third Friday. More information on his availability should come to light as tipoff nears.

signals.detail: Coulibaly will start in Saturday's game against Oklahoma City.

news.headline: Coulibaly will start in Saturday's game against Oklahoma City.
news.story: Coulibaly will make his first start since the 110-102 loss to Charlotte on Oct. 26. In four starts during the 2026-27 campaign, the 22-year-old has averaged 8.0 points, 4.3 rebounds and 1.8 steals over 27.3 minutes per outing.

news.headline: Coulibaly (illness) is available for Wednesday's game against the Hawks.
news.story: Coulibaly is under the weather Wednesday but is giving it a go for the Wizards. Now that AJ Dybantsa's minutes restriction is lifted, Coulibaly could see less playing time going forward.

news.headline: Coulibaly (illness) is questionable for Wednesday against the Hawks.
news.story: Coulibaly was a late addition to the injury report after waking up under the weather. If the Wizards end up holding Coulibaly out, the team could turn more to Khris Middleton and/or Will Riley.

news.headline: Brown, who finished with 18 points (5-13 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 5-7 FT), one rebound, three assists and one steal over 25 minutes in Saturday's 124-121 loss to Atlanta, won't play in Sunday's game against Dallas, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
news.story: Brown logged his fifth consecutive double-digit scoring performance Saturday. However, his efforts weren't enough to help the Nets hold off a late Hawks comeback and earn their third win of the 2026-27 campaign. Head coach Jordi Fernandez mentioned after the game that the rookie won't suit up Sunday versus the Mavericks, the second game of a back-to-back. Without Brown in the lineup, Terance Mann should see more minutes off the bench. Keon Ellis, who didn't get on the floor versus Atlanta, might also get involved.

news.headline: Brown ended with 18 points (6-11 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 3-4 FT), two rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal across 20 minutes during Wednesday's 114-104 win over the Hornets.
news.story: Brown provided an offensive spark off the bench, knocking down three triples while finishing as Brooklyn's third-leading scorer. The rookie also contributed four assists and two defensive stats, though he committed four turnovers. His scoring upside is intriguing, but he'll need more consistent playing time to become a dependable fantasy option.

news.headline: Hyland amassed 19 points (7-13 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds, four assists and one steal across 16 minutes during Wednesday's 117-107 victory over Houston.
news.story: Hyland scored at least 19 points for the second time in the past four games, having now also scored double-digit points in four of the past five games. While he is being asked to do more on the offensive end, his production does seem somewhat unsustainable, especially given his playing time. In four appearances over the past week, he has averaged just 16.0 minutes per game, typically not enough to maintain standard-league relevance.

news.headline: Hyland racked up 19 points (8-16 FG, 3-9 3Pt), eight assists and one steal across 20 minutes during Friday's 127-101 victory over the Clippers.
news.story: Hyland finished just two assists shy of a double-double and recorded his second straight game with double-digit points and over 15 minutes of action. It's still early, but the early signs show Hyland could be in line for a bigger role in the backcourt with Anthony Edwards (knee) sidelined for the foreseeable future.

news.headline: Fantasy Hoops: The Timberwolves players to add in wake of Anthony Edwards injury
news.story: Minnesota Timberwolves guard Anthony Edwards was putting up some of the best numbers of his career before Tuesday's news. Through four games, he averaged 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds and 3.5 assists while shooting 48% from the field. He even scored 47 points in 41 minutes against the Cleveland Cavaliers on Monday despite dealing with knee pain. Now Edwards is scheduled for arthroscopic surgery on his right knee Thursday and could miss around two months. A more definitive return timeline should come after the procedure. Edwards missed a career-high 21 games last season while dealing with knee issu

news.headline: Giddey closed Wednesday's 135-105 loss to the Knicks with 10 points (4-7 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), one rebound and six assists in 27 minutes.
news.story: Giddey was efficient with his limited shot attempts but struggled to make his usual impact on the glass, finishing with just one rebound. The lopsided contest also contributed to a reduced workload for Chicago's starting point guard. Despite the underwhelming performance, Giddey's established role as a primary facilitator should allow him to bounce back in more competitive matchups.

news.headline: Giddey tallied 13 points (5-15 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, 10 assists, a steal and two blocks across 32 minutes in Monday's 126-107 loss to the 76ers.
news.story: Giddey compensated for inefficient shooting with double-digit assists and three steals-plus-blocks, delivering useful fantasy production despite Chicago's struggles. His 10 assists were particularly encouraging given his relatively modest scoring output, making it the third time Giddey has dished out at least 10 assists this season in seven appearances. Giddey's role as the Bulls' primary facilitator continues to support his fantasy value, although inconsistent shooting and fluctuating rebounding totals can limit his ceiling. That said, he's trending in the right direction after averaging 11.8

news.headline: Giddey totaled 13 points (4-8 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four rebounds and five assists across 25 minutes during Friday's 125-111 loss to the Celtics.
news.story: Giddey's 13 points were his most in a game so far this regular season, but he hasn't been able to stuff the stat sheet like he did in each of the two prior seasons. Part of his struggles may be due to a lingering left wrist injury from training camp, although he hasn't shown up on the Bulls' injury report as of late. Giddey's slow start to the season is of some concern, and he'll continue to face tough competition as the Bulls travel to Philadelphia to face the 76ers on Monday.

news.headline: Marshall had 22 points (9-12 FG, 3-3 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, three assists and one block over 26 minutes off the bench during Wednesday's 112-111 loss to the Spurs.
news.story: It was the best performance of the season for the veteran forward, as he set new highs in points, boards and made three-pointers while recording his first block of 2026-27. Marshall missed a few games due to an illness, but in five appearances (one start), he's averaged 13.6 points, 5.4 assists, 3.4 rebounds, 1.4 steals and 1.2 threes in 26.6 minutes while shooting 50.0 percent from the floor.

news.headline: Marshall (illness) is available for Friday's game against Houston.
news.story: Marshall initially drew a questionable tag before being upgraded to probable Friday afternoon, and he's since been cleared to play following a two-game absence. The 28-year-old forward is averaging 13.7 points, 5.7 assists, 3.3 rebounds and 1.7 steals across 27.7 minutes per contest in three regular-season games (one start). With Marshall back in action, Caleb Martin and Zaccharie Risacher could see fewer minutes.

news.headline: Marshall (illness) is probable for Friday's game against the Rockets.
news.story: Marshall is likely to return from a two-game absence Friday. Fewer minutes will likely be available for Zaccharie Risacher off the bench.

news.headline: LaRavia contributed nine points (3-3 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal across 21 minutes during Wednesday's 116-103 victory over Sacramento.
news.story: That's now a fifth straight start for LaRavia, who managed a full stat line Wednesday. He still logged the fewest minutes among Ziaire Williams, Quentin Grimes and Matisse Thybulle, so this appears to be a committee approach for the Lakers' wing minutes.

news.headline: LaRavia registered eight points (3-6 FG, 2-3 3Pt), two rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal in 25 minutes during Sunday's 131-125 win over the Raptors.
news.story: LaRavia delivered a well-rounded performance despite modest scoring, providing two three-pointers and contributions in four additional categories. His starting role offers a path to consistent playing time, though his limited offensive usage caps his upside in standard fantasy formats.

news.headline: LaRavia had two points (1-2 FG), 10 rebounds, two blocks and three steals across 35 minutes during Wednesday's 103-87 win over the Clippers.
news.story: While LaRavia left the scoring to others, the fifth-year forward helped generate extra possessions for the Lakers with his showing on defense, as well as five offensive rebounds. It's the first time LaRavia pulled down double-digit boards since Dec. 20 of last season, also against the Clippers. If Ziaire Williams (foot) misses additional time, LaRavia could remain in the starting five in the short term, but even with a larger workload, he's got limited fantasy appeal.

news.headline: Garland finished with 26 points (10-14 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound and seven assists in 39 minutes during Wednesday's 117-116 overtime loss to Miami.
news.story: Garland bounced back from a 5-of-14 shooting night against Toronto on Monday, leading the Clippers in scoring and tying Rui Hachimura for the team lead in assists. However, turnovers remain a concern for Garland. He committed six Wednesday after giving the ball away seven times Monday. That will cost him in nine-category leagues, but his scoring and playmaking still make him a solid fantasy starter.

news.headline: Garland ended with 16 points (5-14 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 5-6 FT), four rebounds and eight assists in 36 minutes during Monday's 125-118 loss to Toronto.
news.story: Garland led the Clippers in assists but struggled with his efficiency, committing seven turnovers while shooting just 35.7 percent from the field. He also failed to record a steal or block and finished with a team-worst minus-16 rating. The substantial workload and playmaking opportunities remain encouraging, though his turnovers significantly diminished his fantasy production.

news.headline: Antetokounmpo tallied 20 points (7-13 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 5-7 FT), 14 rebounds and four assists across 31 minutes during Thursday's 120-100 loss to the Warriors.
news.story: Antetokounmpo now has six straight regular-season outings with a double-double. He's been stellar to begin his tenure in Miami, and prior to Thursday night's defeat, the Heat had won three of the previous four games. Over Antetokounmpo's last six contests, he's averaging 26.8 points, 15.0 rebounds and 6.8 assists to go along with 1.3 blocks.

news.headline: Antetokounmpo (wrist) is available for Thursday's game against the Warriors, Anthony Chiang of the Miami Herald reports.
news.story: With Miami on the second night of a back-to-back, Antetokounmpo's availability removes any immediate concern about the wrist issue affecting his status Thursday. The star forward should remain in his usual role, though it's worth noting his wrist was heavily taped Wednesday against the Clippers, per Chiang.

signals.detail: If he is unavailable, Tyus Jones could see an expanded role.

news.headline: Murray is questionable for Monday's game against the Rockets due to a left shin contusion.
news.story: Murray could miss his first game of the season due to a right lower leg injury. If he is unavailable, Tyus Jones could see an expanded role.

news.headline: Murray totaled 16 points (6-13 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), eight assists and six rebounds across 34 minutes during Saturday's 114-102 victory over the Pacers.
news.story: Murray was efficient from inside the arc and finished as Denver's third-leading scorer Saturday. The star floor general also tied for the team lead in assists, dishing out at least six dimes for a third consecutive contest. In that stretch, he's averaged 21.7 points, 7.0 assists, 5.3 rebounds and 0.7 steals across 33.7 minutes per tilt.

news.headline: Murray finished with 14 points (4-11 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds, seven assists and a steal across 28 minutes in Wednesday's 128-109 win over the Raptors.
news.story: Murray had a relatively quiet scoring night but contributed effectively as a facilitator, finishing with seven assists and five rebounds. His reduced playing time reflected Denver's comfortable second-half advantage, so fantasy managers shouldn't worry too much about the fact that he didn't reach the 30-minute threshold for the first time this season.

news.headline: Jerome totaled 21 points (7-14 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 5-5 FT), two rebounds and five assists over 28 minutes in Friday's 128-97 loss to the Thunder.
news.story: This was Jerome's third straight 20-plus-point performance, and he scored efficiently, converting half his shots while drilling all five of his freebies. The 29-year-old point guard is having a breakout season, posting top-25 value behind averages of 26.6 points, 5.3 assists, 2.5 triples and 0.9 steals per game on 50.3 percent shooting from the field and 88.2 percent at the line.

news.headline: Jerome notched 23 points (10-20 FG, 2-10 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, three assists and a block across 29 minutes in Wednesday's 107-103 loss to the Pacers.
news.story: Jerome tied for Memphis' scoring lead despite struggling from beyond the arc, making just two of 10 three-point attempts. His 20 field-goal attempts once again showed the prominent role he has on offense for the Grizzlies, although four turnovers diminished his fantasy production. Jerome's scoring opportunities provide meaningful upside, and he's enjoying an outstanding start to the season with averages of 27.4 points, 3.6 rebounds and 5.3 assists per contest.

news.headline: Queen contributed 20 points (8-21 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 4-4 FT), nine rebounds, six assists and one block across 27 minutes off the bench in Wednesday's 120-113 overtime win over the Jazz.
news.story: Queen didn't deliver his most efficient shooting performance but wasn't shy about hunting his shot en route to a season-high-tying scoring total. The second-year center also led the Pelicans in rebounds and assists, dishing out a season-high six dimes. He's scored 20 points in back-to-back outings and will likely continue seeing increased burn in Yves Missi's (knee) stead.

news.headline: Queen notched 20 points (7-13 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), seven rebounds, five assists, one block and two steals across 24 minutes during Monday's 135-134 overtime victory over Memphis.
news.story: Queen continued to come off the bench, yet put together another intriguing performance. The fact that he has not been inserted into the starting lineup despite an injury to Yves Missi (knee) indicates that the coaching staff is not comfortable playing him for more than about 25 minutes on any given night. While this does limit his overall upside, he is doing more than enough in a bench role to be considered a must-roster player.

news.headline: Queen posted eight points (3-6 FG, 2-2 FT), eight rebounds, four assists and one steal in 23 minutes during Saturday's 121-99 win over Atlanta.
news.story: Queen finished Saturday's game as the Pelicans' second-leading bench scorer and finished second on the team in rebounds behind Karlo Matkovic (10). Although he's coming off the bench, Queen's averages early on in the 2026-27 season are similar to what he produced during his rookie campaign last year. The Maryland product is averaging 11.2 points, 7.8 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 1.0 steals over 23.7 minutes per game this season.

news.headline: Knueppel (hamstring) was diagnosed with a left hamstring strain Sunday and will be re-evaluated in four weeks.
news.story: Knueppel missed the first eight games of the 2026-27 campaign. He returned for the 114-104 loss to Brooklyn on Wednesday, though he exited the contest after just six minutes of work and didn't return. With Knueppel out of commission for at least a month, Grayson Allen and Sion James are candidates to replace him in the starting lineup, especially with Dennis Schroder (hamstring) sidelined for a minimum of two weeks.

news.headline: Knueppel (hamstring) is out for Friday's game against the Celtics.
news.story: Knueppel aggravated his left hamstring strain in his season debut Wednesday against Brooklyn. The Hornets haven't yet indicated whether the sharpshooter is facing a multi-week absence, but they'll likely proceed with caution. Grayson Allen is back in the mix as a high-end fantasy streaming option for as long as Knueppel is out.

news.headline: Knueppel exited Wednesday's game against the Nets after experiencing soreness in his left leg, and he will not return, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
news.story: This is the same leg that delayed Knueppel's season debut, but for now the team is calling it a leg injury rather than specifically citing his hamstring. Still, it's concerning that he seemingly suffered a non-contact injury after just six minutes of play. For now, Knueppel should be considered questionable for Friday's meeting with the Celtics.

news.headline: Harris (calf) is listed as out for Saturday's game against Minnesota.
news.story: Harris suffered a strained left calf ahead of the 2026-27 campaign and has yet to make his debut with the Spurs. The veteran is slowly making progress toward a return, though he should be considered week-to-week until more information is released. The 34-year-old, who signed with San Antonio during the offseason, averaged 13.3 points, 5.1 rebounds and 2.5 assists over 27.7 minutes per contest in 63 regular-season appearances with the Pistons in 2025-26.

news.headline: Harris (calf) is out for Wednesday's game against Utah, Paul Garcia of ProjectSpurs.com reports.
news.story: This will be Harris' fifth straight game on the shelf as the Spurs continue to wait for his official debut. Harris is progressing and is said to be close to day-to-day.

news.headline: Harris (calf) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Kings.
news.story: Harris is still ramping up from a left calf strain and will miss a fourth consecutive contest to begin the regular season. His next opportunity to make his season debut will come Wednesday at Utah in the second leg of this back-to-back set. Julian Champagnie and Keldon Johnson will likely continue seeing increased playing time while Harris is sidelined. "He's progressing on the court, and it's going well," Spurs head coach Mitch Johnson said about Harris' return timeline. "We're excited to have him back very soon."

news.headline: Sheppard (back) is available for Monday's matchup with Boston, Will Guillory of The Athletic reports.
news.story: Sheppard will return from a two-game absence due to a lower-back strain. The third-year guard is averaging 10.5 points, 4.8 assists, 2.8 rebounds and 1.8 steals across 23.3 minutes per game in four regular-season outings (one start), and his return will leave fewer minutes available for Bogdan Bogdanovic.

news.headline: Sheppard (back) is questionable for Monday's game against the Celtics.
news.story: Sheppard is in danger of missing his fourth game of the 2026-27 campaign. With Fred VanVleet (knee) not listed on the injury report, Marcus Smart could continue to be more involved than usual if Sheppard can't suit up Monday.

news.headline: Sheppard (back) is out for Saturday's game against the Thunder.
news.story: This will be Sheppard's second straight game on the sidelines, and for now, he should be viewed as questionable for Monday's game against the Celtics. Fred VanVleet (knee) will join Sheppard on the inactive list for Saturday's game, paving the way for Marcus Smart to start.

news.headline: Ingram (Achilles) won't play in Sunday's game against New Orleans, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
news.story: Ingram hasn't played yet this season. While the veteran is reportedly moving in a positive direction, he won't make his 2026-27 campaign debut Sunday versus his former team. Ingram's next opportunity to suit up will come Tuesday in Phoenix. In the meantime, Darius Garland will remain the Clippers' No. 1 scoring option.

news.headline: Ingram (Achilles) has progressed to full contact basketball activities, per NBA writer Justin Russo.
news.story: Ingram told reporters Friday he's close to returning, though a concrete timeline for his season debut has yet to be disclosed. The star forward is recovering from a partial Achilles tear, and it sounds like he'll be ready to roll at some point in mid-November.

news.headline: Antetokounmpo (wrist) is available for Thursday's game against the Warriors, Anthony Chiang of the Miami Herald reports.
news.story: With Miami on the second night of a back-to-back, Antetokounmpo's availability removes any immediate concern about the wrist issue affecting his status Thursday. The star forward should remain in his usual role, though it's worth noting his wrist was heavily taped Wednesday against the Clippers, per Chiang.

news.headline: LaRavia contributed nine points (3-3 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal across 21 minutes during Wednesday's 116-103 victory over Sacramento.
news.story: That's now a fifth straight start for LaRavia, who managed a full stat line Wednesday. He still logged the fewest minutes among Ziaire Williams, Quentin Grimes and Matisse Thybulle, so this appears to be a committee approach for the Lakers' wing minutes.

news.headline: LaRavia registered eight points (3-6 FG, 2-3 3Pt), two rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal in 25 minutes during Sunday's 131-125 win over the Raptors.
news.story: LaRavia delivered a well-rounded performance despite modest scoring, providing two three-pointers and contributions in four additional categories. His starting role offers a path to consistent playing time, though his limited offensive usage caps his upside in standard fantasy formats.

news.headline: LaRavia had two points (1-2 FG), 10 rebounds, two blocks and three steals across 35 minutes during Wednesday's 103-87 win over the Clippers.
news.story: While LaRavia left the scoring to others, the fifth-year forward helped generate extra possessions for the Lakers with his showing on defense, as well as five offensive rebounds. It's the first time LaRavia pulled down double-digit boards since Dec. 20 of last season, also against the Clippers. If Ziaire Williams (foot) misses additional time, LaRavia could remain in the starting five in the short term, but even with a larger workload, he's got limited fantasy appeal.

news.headline: Giddey closed Wednesday's 135-105 loss to the Knicks with 10 points (4-7 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), one rebound and six assists in 27 minutes.
news.story: Giddey was efficient with his limited shot attempts but struggled to make his usual impact on the glass, finishing with just one rebound. The lopsided contest also contributed to a reduced workload for Chicago's starting point guard. Despite the underwhelming performance, Giddey's established role as a primary facilitator should allow him to bounce back in more competitive matchups.

news.headline: Giddey tallied 13 points (5-15 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, 10 assists, a steal and two blocks across 32 minutes in Monday's 126-107 loss to the 76ers.
news.story: Giddey compensated for inefficient shooting with double-digit assists and three steals-plus-blocks, delivering useful fantasy production despite Chicago's struggles. His 10 assists were particularly encouraging given his relatively modest scoring output, making it the third time Giddey has dished out at least 10 assists this season in seven appearances. Giddey's role as the Bulls' primary facilitator continues to support his fantasy value, although inconsistent shooting and fluctuating rebounding totals can limit his ceiling. news.headline: Giddey totaled 13 points (4-8 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four rebounds and five assists across 25 minutes during Friday's 125-111 loss to the Celtics.
news.story: Giddey's 13 points were his most in a game so far this regular season, but he hasn't been able to stuff the stat sheet like he did in each of the two prior seasons. Part of his struggles may be due to a lingering left wrist injury from training camp, although he hasn't shown up on the Bulls' injury report as of late. Giddey's slow start to the season is of some concern, and he'll continue to face tough competition as the Bulls travel to Philadelphia to face the 76ers on Monday.

news.headline: Marshall had 22 points (9-12 FG, 3-3 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, three assists and one block over 26 minutes off the bench during Wednesday's 112-111 loss to the Spurs.
news.story: It was the best performance of the season for the veteran forward, as he set new highs in points, boards and made three-pointers while recording his first block of 2026-27. Marshall missed a few games due to an illness, but in five appearances (one start), he's averaged 13.6 points, 5.4 assists, 3.4 rebounds, 1.4 steals and 1.2 threes in 26.6 minutes while shooting 50.0 percent from the floor.

news.headline: Marshall (illness) is available for Friday's game against Houston.
news.story: Marshall initially drew a questionable tag before being upgraded to probable Friday afternoon, and he's since been cleared to play following a two-game absence. The 28-year-old forward is averaging 13.7 points, 5.7 assists, 3.3 rebounds and 1.7 steals across 27.7 minutes per contest in three regular-season games (one start). With Marshall back in action, Caleb Martin and Zaccharie Risacher could see fewer minutes.

news.headline: Marshall (illness) is probable for Friday's game against the Rockets.
news.story: Marshall is likely to return from a two-game absence Friday. Fewer minutes will likely be available for Zaccharie Risacher off the bench.

news.headline: Sheppard (back) is available for Monday's matchup with Boston, Will Guillory of The Athletic reports.
news.story: Sheppard will return from a two-game absence due to a lower-back strain. The third-year guard is averaging 10.5 points, 4.8 assists, 2.8 rebounds and 1.8 steals across 23.3 minutes per game in four regular-season outings (one start), and his return will leave fewer minutes available for Bogdan Bogdanovic.

news.headline: Sheppard (back) is questionable for Monday's game against the Celtics.
news.story: Sheppard is in danger of missing his fourth game of the 2026-27 campaign. With Fred VanVleet (knee) not listed on the injury report, Marcus Smart could continue to be more involved than usual if Sheppard can't suit up Monday.

news.headline: Sheppard (back) is out for Saturday's game against the Thunder.
news.story: This will be Sheppard's second straight game on the sidelines, and for now, he should be viewed as questionable for Monday's game against the Celtics. Fred VanVleet (knee) will join Sheppard on the inactive list for Saturday's game, paving the way for Marcus Smart to start.

news.headline: Jerome totaled 21 points (7-14 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 5-5 FT), two rebounds and five assists over 28 minutes in Friday's 128-97 loss to the Thunder.
news.story: This was Jerome's third straight 20-plus-point performance, and he scored efficiently, converting half his shots while drilling all five of his freebies. The 29-year-old point guard is having a breakout season, posting top-25 value behind averages of 26.6 points, 5.3 assists, 2.5 triples and 0.9 steals per game on 50.3 percent shooting from the field and 88.2 percent at the line.

news.headline: Jerome notched 23 points (10-20 FG, 2-10 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, three assists and a block across 29 minutes in Wednesday's 107-103 loss to the Pacers.
news.story: Jerome tied for Memphis' scoring lead despite struggling from beyond the arc, making just two of 10 three-point attempts. His 20 field-goal attempts once again showed the prominent role he has on offense for the Grizzlies, although four turnovers diminished his fantasy production. Jerome's scoring opportunities provide meaningful upside, and he's enjoying an outstanding start to the season with averages of 27.4 points, 3.6 rebounds and 5.3 assists per contest.
